related.why: The same lump description, applied to the neck

brief.scenario: Mrs Hughes, 45, noticed a swelling in the front of her neck three months ago. She has been referred by her GP.
brief.task: Examine her neck. You will be stopped at 6 minutes to present your findings and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Does it move on swallowing, what are her nodes doing, and is she euthyroid?
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Palpating only from the front and forgetting the swallow during palpation.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Put a glass of water within reach before you start.

grid.label: Preparation
grid.fail: Starts palpating without introduction, consent or hand hygiene.
grid.pass: Introduces, confirms identity, explains, gains consent, cleans hands; exposes the neck to the clavicles with the patient seated.
grid.high: Asks about pain before touching, and has water ready for the swallow test.

grid.label: Inspection
grid.fail: Inspects without the swallow or tongue test.
grid.pass: Inspects from the front; swallow test (thyroid moves up) and tongue protrusion (thyroglossal cyst moves up).
grid.high: Adds inspection from the side, and looks for scars and dilated neck veins.

grid.label: Palpation
grid.fail: Palpates from the front only, or misses the lymph nodes.
grid.borderline: Palpates from behind but doesn't ask her to swallow while palpating.
grid.pass: From behind: each lobe and the isthmus, with a swallow; then the cervical lymph nodes.
grid.high: Describes the lump fully (site, size, surface, consistency, mobility) and checks tracheal position.

grid.label: Retrosternal extension
grid.fail: Omits any assessment for retrosternal extension.
grid.pass: Percusses over the manubrium and listens for a bruit.
grid.high: Performs Pemberton's test: facial plethora when both arms are raised suggests retrosternal extension.

grid.label: Thyroid status
grid.pass: Pulse, hands (tremor, sweating), eyes (lid lag, exophthalmos) and reflexes.
grid.high: Adds eye movements for ophthalmoplegia, and proximal myopathy by standing from a chair with arms crossed.

grid.label: Presentation at the signal
grid.fail: Lists actions rather than findings, or runs past the signal.
grid.pass: Summarises the findings concisely and gives a most likely diagnosis with a differential.
grid.high: Leads with the key finding, states the important negatives (nodes, retrosternal extension, thyroid signs), then commits.

grid.label: Investigation and referral
grid.pass: TSH, ultrasound, and ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration if ultrasound features warrant it.
grid.high: Names red flags (stridor, voice change, rapid growth, cervical nodes) and a suspected cancer pathway referral for an unexplained thyroid lump.

grid.label: Closing
grid.fail: Leaves without thanking her or cleaning hands.
grid.pass: Thanks her, checks she is comfortable, cleans hands.
grid.high: Says what else they would examine, e.g. a full cardiovascular examination if the pulse is irregular.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Starts palpating the neck from the front straight away.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: There's a lump on the right. It's probably a goitre.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Please stop there. What are your findings?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I felt her neck and looked at it, and I'd like to feel it more.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel, one of the surgical trainees. Can I check your name and date of birth? I'd like to examine your neck; is that all right? Any pain? [Cleans hands.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Inspects from the front.] Could you take a sip of water and hold it… now swallow. And stick your tongue out for me.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [From behind.] I'm going to feel your neck now. Another sip and swallow, please. [Then the cervical nodes.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Pulse; hands; eyes for lid lag and exophthalmos; reflexes.]

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Please stop. What are your findings?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mrs Hughes has a 2 cm swelling in the right lobe that moves on swallowing but not with tongue protrusion. It's smooth and firm. No lymph nodes, no retrosternal extension, and she's clinically euthyroid. This is most likely a solitary thyroid nodule; the differential is a colloid nodule, adenoma, cyst or carcinoma.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: TSH, then ultrasound, with ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration if the ultrasound features warrant it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel, one of the surgical trainees. Can I check your name and date of birth? I'd like to look at and feel your neck, and check a few things like your pulse and eyes; is that all right? Is your neck sore anywhere? [Cleans hands; water within reach.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Inspects from the front and side: no scars or dilated veins.] A sip of water, hold it… swallow. Now stick your tongue out.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [From behind, each lobe and the isthmus, with a swallow.] [Cervical nodes.] [Checks the trachea is central.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Percusses the manubrium; auscultates.] Could you raise both arms above your head and hold them there? [Watches the face.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Pulse, hands, lid lag, exophthalmos, eye movements.] Could you stand up from the chair with your arms crossed? [Reflexes.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Thank you. I'd also like to complete a full cardiovascular examination if her pulse were irregular. [Cleans hands.]

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Please stop. What are your findings?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A solitary nodule in the right lobe: about 2 cm, smooth, firm, moving on swallowing but not with tongue protrusion. The trachea is central. Importantly, there are no palpable nodes, no signs of retrosternal extension and no signs of thyroid dysfunction. My working diagnosis is a solitary thyroid nodule, and I need to exclude carcinoma.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How would you investigate, and what would worry you?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: TSH, ultrasound, and ultrasound-guided FNA if the features warrant it. Stridor, a change in voice, rapid growth or cervical nodes would worry me. An unexplained thyroid lump should be considered for a suspected cancer pathway referral.

failures.consequence: Misses a goitre that can compress the trachea or great veins.

failures.move: Examining the lump but not thyroid status.
failures.consequence: A toxic nodule changes both the investigation and the management.
Loses the closing courtesy and the chance to say what else you'd examine.

recovery.when: You forgot the swallow during palpation
recovery.line: Could I ask you to swallow once more while I feel from behind?

recovery.when: You're asked something you can't answer
recovery.line: I'm not certain. I'd start with TSH and an ultrasound, and discuss the result with my senior.

knowledge.fact: Moves on swallowing: thyroid. Moves with tongue protrusion: thyroglossal cyst.
Pemberton's sign: facial plethora on raising both arms suggests retrosternal extension.
Offer ultrasound for palpable thyroid enlargement when malignancy is suspected; use ultrasound guidance for FNA.
Consider a suspected cancer pathway referral for an unexplained thyroid lump.

recall.think: Is it thyroid, is it one nodule, and is anything pressing or spreading?
recall.say: "A sip of water, hold it… now swallow."
recall.finish: TSH, ultrasound ± guided FNA; suspected cancer pathway if unexplained.

partner.opening: Please examine this patient's neck. I'll stop you at 6 minutes to present.
partner.actorBrief: You are Mrs Hughes, 45. You noticed the lump three months ago; it isn't painful. Swallow when asked. If asked about symptoms: no voice change, no difficulty breathing, no weight loss or palpitations.

reveals.trigger: Inspects and asks her to swallow
reveals.finding: A swelling in the right side of the neck rises on swallowing.

reveals.trigger: Asks her to protrude her tongue

reveals.finding: Right lobe: a 2 cm smooth, firm nodule. No other nodules. Trachea central.
Resonant manubrium, no bruit, Pemberton's negative.
Pulse 72 regular; no tremor, lid lag or exophthalmos; normal reflexes.
Say: "Please stop there and present your findings."

push.question: How would you investigate?
push.expect: TSH, ultrasound, ultrasound-guided FNA if indicated.

push.question: What would make this urgent?
push.expect: Stridor, voice change, rapid growth, nodes; suspected cancer pathway.

curveballs.prompt: She now tells you her voice has become hoarse.
curveballs.safeAnswer: That's a red flag for recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement: suspected cancer pathway referral.
Possible AF from thyrotoxicosis: check TSH and complete a cardiovascular examination.

curveballs.prompt: The swelling moves up when she sticks out her tongue.
curveballs.safeAnswer: That suggests a thyroglossal cyst rather than a thyroid nodule.
